title: Arriving From Between
notes: DP-expanded version. All parent locations now carry DP-level sub-locations — specific camera positions, surfaces, and objects visible in frame. Hotel_New_Yorker_1943 expanded to 7 sub-locations (5 new, 2 existing). Smiljan_Village_1856 expanded to 12 sub-locations (9 new, 3 existing). Gospic_Valley_1856 expanded to 4 sub-locations (2 new, 2 existing). Hotel_St_Regis_1922 expanded to 3 sub-locations (all new). Port_Of_New_York_1884 expanded to 2 sub-locations. Wardenclyffe_Evidence_1943 expanded to 3 sub-locations. All 15 characters and 15 objects preserved exactly from prior version.

assets.name: Alice_Monaghan_1943
assets.physique: Irish-American woman, late 30s, medium build, dark hair pinned under a white maid's cap, practical posture, composed expression trained by years of hotel service
assets.attire: Hotel New Yorker maid uniform — white blouse, black dress, white apron, white cap, black leather shoes
assets.notes: Housekeeping staff. Found Tesla's body on the morning of January 8, 1943. Smelled the ozone before she crossed the threshold. Told no one officially except her sister, once.

assets.name: Nikola_Tesla_1943
assets.notes: Age 86. Final day. Found dead in Room 3327, Hotel New Yorker. Sheets pulled to military tightness. Three gray-tipped feathers on the windowsill. Hotel napkins covered in equations on the desk.

assets.name: Nikola_Tesla_1856
assets.physique: Newborn infant, pale skin, dark hair, eyes open at the moment of birth
assets.notes: Born at stroke of midnight during a violent lightning storm in Smiljan. FLUX cannot render infant Tesla from training data — needs description.

assets.name: Nikola_Tesla_1859
assets.physique: Serbian boy, approximately 3 years old, slight frame, dark hair, large dark eyes, small hands spread flat on the cat's back
assets.attire: Simple linen shirt, loose trousers, bare feet
assets.notes: The cat scene. Pulled a sheet of sparks from Macak's back in a dark room. Responded with a question, not fear. FLUX needs description for child-age Tesla.

assets.name: Nikola_Tesla_1862
assets.physique: Serbian boy, approximately 6 years old, thin build, dark hair, intense focused eyes, holding a tin fork at the dinner table
assets.attire: Simple linen shirt, braces, dark trousers
assets.notes: The geometry vision scene. Fork in hand at dinner table when the visual field was replaced by luminous squares. FLUX needs description for child-age Tesla.

assets.name: Nikola_Tesla_1884
assets.notes: Age 28. Arrived at Port of New York with four cents and a letter of introduction to Thomas Edison.

assets.name: Duka_Tesla_1856
assets.physique: Serbian woman, mid-30s, strong peasant build, dark hair pulled back tightly, weathered hands, intense dark eyes, high cheekbones, broad shoulders from farm work
assets.attire: Simple white linen dress for childbirth, wool blanket over shoulders
assets.notes: Tesla's mother, née Mandic. Known for exceptional memory — could recite Serbian epic poetry at length. Built her own household tools. Gripped the wooden headboard rail during labor with the focus of someone doing something with all of themselves.

assets.name: Milutin_Tesla_1856
assets.physique: Serbian Orthodox priest, late 30s, tall, lean build, full dark beard, deep-set eyes, high forehead, scholarly bearing
assets.attire: Black Orthodox clerical robe with silver cross pendant
assets.notes: Tesla's father. Parish priest of Smiljan. Spoke four languages. Could parse Greek and Latin scripture. Named what his son pulled from the cat's back: electricity. The same thing as lightning.

assets.name: The_Midwife_1856
assets.physique: Croatian village woman, approximately 61 years old, stout and sturdy build, grey hair beneath a white kerchief, calloused hands, practical weathered face, expression of someone who has seen the work of birth and death without flinching
assets.attire: Simple brown wool dress, white apron, leather shoes
assets.notes: Unnamed village midwife who delivered Tesla. Had lived on the Lika plateau for 61 years. Hair on her forearms stood straight up crossing the threshold. Sparks jumped from her skirts with every step. Described to her daughter that the smell in the house was the smell of lightning that had already struck — while the lightning was still in the sky.

assets.name: Zdravko_Blazic_1856
assets.physique: Croatian schoolteacher, mid-30s, lean build, neat dark hair, ink-stained fingers, observant eyes behind a practical expression, the look of a man trained to write down what he sees
assets.attire: Simple wool coat, white shirt, dark trousers, leather boots
assets.notes: Schoolteacher in Gospic valley, 15 kilometers below Smiljan. Kept a meticulous diary of weather, road conditions, and livestock. His July 1856 entry described livestock standing in open fields facing the same direction, the well water tasting different, and the morning light looking like an examination being conducted. The exact date is water-damaged in the surviving page.

assets.name: Subject_K_1974
assets.physique: Croatian woman, approximately 80 years old, small and thin, white hair, careful deliberate speech, the bearing of someone carrying something she has been deciding whether to pass on for decades
assets.attire: Simple dark dress, wool shawl, practical shoes
assets.notes: Identified only as Subject K. in a 1974 cassette interview with a graduate student from the University of Zagreb. Third-generation memory carrier. Her grandmother was a young woman from Gospic in 1856 who described the sky looking clean in a way it hadn't been before the morning after Tesla's birth. Died before 1990. No family named.

assets.name: Dane_Tesla_1863
assets.physique: Serbian boy, approximately 12 years old, taller and heavier than Nikola, dark hair, confident bearing of the celebrated eldest son
assets.attire: Simple linen shirt, dark trousers, worn leather shoes that had been broken in precisely to his foot's shape
assets.notes: Tesla's older brother. Died in a horse accident in Smiljan, approximately 1863-1865 (sources disagree). His coat remained on the hook by the door. His shoes held the shape of a foot that would not return. After his death, Tesla's visions intensified in frequency and vividness.

assets.name: Walter_Simmons_1943
assets.physique: American man, early 40s, medium build, practical work-worn face, steady observant eyes, the unhurried bearing of someone who has walked the same building corridors for years
assets.attire: Hotel maintenance uniform — grey coveralls or work trousers and jacket, heavy leather work boots
assets.notes: Maintenance worker at the Hotel New Yorker from approximately 1935 to 1950. Kept a diary of the building's physical life. In January 1943, during routine rounds on the 33rd floor, smelled ozone in the corridor near Room 3327 despite it being January with no storm. Noted it in his diary and walked on. His diary ends with that January 1943 entry. His initials and partial diary survive in a typescript provided to a researcher in the 1960s; the researcher died before the book was published. The foundation holding the estate papers does not maintain a public finding aid.

assets.name: PE_Foxworth_1943
assets.physique: American man, late 30s, clean-shaven, sharp jaw, close-cropped dark hair, military bearing in a civilian suit, alert eyes that do not settle
assets.attire: Dark grey wool suit, white shirt, narrow tie, fedora, leather briefcase
assets.notes: FBI Assistant Director. Head of the Special Intelligence Service. Was involved from early on January 7, 1943 — before Tesla's body was publicly reported. His timeline of involvement precedes the publicly established discovery timeline.

assets.name: John_G_Trump_1943
assets.physique: American man, mid-30s, round face, receding hairline, wire-rimmed glasses, academic softness, mild expression that does not match the weight of what he was asked to evaluate
assets.attire: Tweed suit jacket, bow tie, white shirt, leather oxfords
assets.notes: MIT physicist assigned to review Tesla's seized papers. Reviewed 60 years of work in three weeks. Concluded the material did not include new workable principles for scientific or military application and would not constitute a hazard in unfriendly hands. The material was then classified for decades.

assets.name: Hotel_New_Yorker_1943
assets.physique: Art deco hotel, 43 stories, corner of 34th Street and 8th Avenue, Manhattan. Tesla's home for his final decade, given to him at a nominal or free rate in exchange for the distinction of his residence.
assets.notes: Parent location — use sub-locations for all scene-level shots.

children.name: Room_3327_1943
children.physique: Corner room on the 33rd floor. Wide establishing shot from the doorway takes in the full room: heavy curtains still against cold winter light, dark wood desk positioned near the window, single bed against the north wall, sheets pulled to military tightness. Hotel napkins stacked on desk and bedside table and scattered on the floor, covered in dense mathematical notation that crosses the paper edges without registering them as limits. Radiator ticking beneath the window. Three gray-tipped feathers on the windowsill, arranged as if placed. The room colder than the corridor — the cold of a space that has not had a living body moving through it. The air carries the smell of a summer storm in January.
children.notes: Wide establishing shot of the full room from doorway. Room number divisible by 3 — Tesla's requirement. The window was left open for the white pigeon. The Do Not Disturb sign had been on the door for three days before Monaghan opened it.

children.name: Room_3327_Desk_Area_1943
children.physique: Dark wood writing desk positioned near the window of Room 3327. Camera framed on the desk surface and the window behind it. The desk surface completely obscured by dozens of white hotel napkins covered in dense mathematical notation in pencil — a handwriting that crosses the printed borders of the napkins without adjusting, treating the paper's edges as limits the mind declined to recognize. A draft from the window left open in January stirs the napkins slightly. Pencil stubs, a magnifying lens, a water glass with a residue ring. The desk lamp unlit. Natural winter light from the window falling across the equations. The windowsill with three gray-tipped feathers visible at the periphery of frame.
children.notes: The desk is where Tesla did his final work. The napkins are the only writing surface available in quantity. The equations are real mathematics — active scientific work, not scribbling. The desk appears in close-ups AND in wider room shots — must be visually consistent in both.

children.name: Room_3327_Windowsill_1943
children.physique: Camera pointed directly at the windowsill of Room 3327, wide enough to hold objects. Three gray-tipped feathers lying at angles that suggest placement — deliberate, considered arrangement, not the casual landing of shed feathers. The window itself slightly ajar despite January cold, heavy curtains hanging still on either side. Through the gap: the grey winter light of Manhattan morning, the geometry of buildings across 8th Avenue. Condensation on the glass where warm room air meets cold window. The radiator ticking beneath, its iron surface patinated with decades of repainting.
children.notes: The window was left open for the white pigeon. She was not coming back. He knew she was not coming back. The feathers were on the windowsill despite the window being closed and undisturbed when Monaghan entered — but Tesla had been keeping the window open for years. The feathers are from a pigeon dead for approximately 20 years.

children.name: Room_3327_Bed_1943
children.physique: Camera framed on the single bed against the north wall of Room 3327. Sheets pulled to a specific tightness — not hotel housekeeping tightness but the precision of someone who understood this would be the last arrangement and made it accordingly. White linens, thin wool blanket folded with geometric exactness. A bedside table with more hotel napkins covered in equations. On the floor beside the bed: additional napkins, some crumpled, some laid flat as if referenced during the night. The pillow showing the slight depression of a head that rested with intention.
children.notes: The body was arranged with a precision that did not suggest rest. Alice Monaghan's professional composure broke here — not dramatically, not with sound, but in a breath.

children.name: Room_3327_Door_Threshold_1943
children.physique: Camera positioned just inside the doorway of Room 3327, looking inward — the view Alice Monaghan had when the door swung open. The Do Not Disturb sign hanging from the interior brass handle. Corridor light spilling in behind the camera position, mixing with the cold winter light from the window ahead. The full depth of the room visible in a single shot: desk to the left near the window, bed against the far wall. The smell — sharp, clean, metallic — moving outward through the open door into the corridor as if concentrated air finding an opening.
children.notes: This is the threshold moment — the boundary between the ordinary hotel corridor and whatever was in that room. The smell did not wait for her to step into it. It stepped into her.

children.name: Hotel_Corridor_33rd_Floor_1943
children.physique: Long narrow hallway, repeating pattern of dark wood doors. Geometric carpet in muted burgundy and gold. Flat institutional lighting from wall sconces. Brass room numbers on each door. Quiet. Still. The smell of ozone detectable near Room 3327 — the kind of smell that arrives after a summer storm — in a building with sealed windows in January.
children.notes: Where Walter Simmons noticed the smell during his regular maintenance rounds.

children.name: Hotel_New_Yorker_Exterior_1943
children.physique: 43-story art deco tower at the corner of 34th Street and 8th Avenue. Brick and limestone facade with strong vertical emphasis. Hotel New Yorker signage near the crown. Street-level awnings. January snow on sidewalks. Yellow taxicabs on 8th Avenue. Pedestrians in winter overcoats and hats.

assets.name: Smiljan_Village_1856
assets.physique: Small village on a high limestone plateau in the Lika region of the Austrian Empire's Military Frontier. Rocky karst landscape, cold even in summer. Stone farmhouses with dark timber roofs and whitewashed walls. A single road through the village. A Serbian Orthodox parish church at the center. Wild thyme growing between the stones. Summer night — dense warm air, limestone dust smell, distant thunder.
assets.notes: Modern-day Croatia. Population under 400 in 1856. The Tesla family farmhouse was adjacent to the parish church where Milutin Tesla served as priest. Parent location — use sub-locations for all scene-level shots.

children.name: Tesla_Farmhouse_Smiljan_1856
children.physique: Simple stone farmhouse with whitewashed walls and dark timber roof. Small windows with wooden shutters. Bare earth yard. Oil lamp light visible through the window. The smell of the storm outside penetrating the walls — sharp, clean, electric. Interior: rough stone walls, low timber ceilings, oil lamp casting uneven light.
children.notes: Exterior establishing shot of the farmhouse where Tesla was born at the stroke of midnight, July 10, 1856, during a violent lightning storm.

children.name: Birthing_Room_Headboard_Corner_1856
children.physique: Camera framed on the corner of the birthing room dominated by the wooden headboard of the bed. Duka Tesla's hands gripping the rail — not the grip of a frightened woman but of someone doing something with all of themselves. The wood worn smooth where hands have gripped before, the grain polished by contact. Sparks jumping from nearby fabric to the wood surface — small bright arcs in the charged air. The single oil lamp casting shadows on the rough stone wall behind the headboard. The midwife's form partially visible at the edge of frame, hands in position.
children.notes: Close-to-medium shot. The headboard rail is the primary visual anchor. Camera is intimate, not observational — inside the room, inside the event.

children.name: Birthing_Room_Threshold_1856
children.physique: Camera pointed at the stone doorway of the birthing room — the threshold the midwife crossed when the hair on her forearms stood up. The stone doorframe, rough-hewn and thick. Wooden floorboards at the threshold showing burn-marks where sparks jumped from her skirts with every step she took across it. The transition from the dark corridor behind the camera position to the lamp-lit room ahead. The air in the doorway visible as something thick — charged, pressurized, resisting breath. Through the doorway: the bed, the lamp, the occupied room. The smell of lightning that has already struck while the storm is still outside.
children.notes: The threshold is a camera position, not just a physical feature. The corridor is dark, the birthing room is lit. The doorway is the frame within the frame.

children.name: Birthing_Room_Oil_Lamp_Corner_1856
children.physique: Camera framed on the single oil lamp on a wooden stand near the washing basin in the corner of the birthing room. The lamp flame steady despite the charged air — it does not gutter or flicker. Rough stone walls catching uneven amber light, the shadows long and warm against cold stone. The washing basin beside the stand: water, clean linens folded in the practical arrangement of a woman who has done this work before. Shadows cast long across the floor toward the bed. The practical tools of birth arranged within arm's reach of where they are needed.
children.notes: This is the calm-within-the-storm shot. The lamp is steady. The arrangement is practical. The work knows what it is doing even when the room does not.

children.name: Tesla_Dark_Room_Before_Sparks_1859
children.physique: Complete interior darkness. Camera close on the tactile: a three-year-old's small hands spread flat on a large cat's back. The fur warm under small palms, parting slightly under the pressure of small fingers. The body warmth of a living animal rising through the fur into the hands. No light source visible. Only the surface under the hands, the warmth, and the darkness that has not yet changed.
children.notes: The moment before the discharge. No visible room details — this is pre-event darkness. The cat's fur and the child's hands are the only visible elements. Shot is intimate and still.

children.name: Tesla_Dark_Room_Discharge_1859
children.physique: The same dark room in the instant of the discharge. A continuous sheet of blue-white sparks fanning across the entire back of the cat from the base of the tail to the neck — not a single spark but a sustained sheet of light. The room lit from beneath, from the interface between fur and palm. The child's own small hands visible from the inside — small finger bones silhouetted in the blue-white light rising from the animal under his hands. The room revealed for one instant in the discharge light: stone walls, timber ceiling, the ordinary room now extraordinary from its floor up. Then darkness again.
children.notes: The moment of discharge. The light source is from below — from the contact surface. This is the shot that inverts normal illumination. Must be visually distinct from any standard scene lighting.

children.name: Tesla_Dining_Table_1862
children.physique: Camera framed on the family dining room table set for a meal. Tin utensils, plates, the clutter of a family in active use of a surface. A boy of approximately 6 years old holding a tin fork — thumb resting on the seam where handle meets tines. The room warm from lamp and bodies, occupied, ordinary. Duka's face visible across the table with the expression of a woman who has already watched her son's eyes go somewhere before and knows what she is about to watch happen again.
children.notes: The moment before the geometry vision. The fork is in hand. The table is real. The room is real. This is the last ordinary moment before the visual field is replaced entirely.

children.name: Tesla_Fork_Vision_1862
children.physique: The dining room replaced entirely. The visual field not interrupted but overwritten — perfect luminous squares tessellated across every visible surface, arriving without transition, so geometrically complete they displace the actual surroundings without remainder. Blinding white-gold light, organized into geometry, the squares fitting against each other without gaps across the entire field of view. The fork still present — held in a hand that is somewhere that is not the dinner table — but the table itself gone, the family gone, replaced by the geometry that has arrived to show itself.
children.notes: Atmosphere scene — no physical location reference, pure geometry. The fork may be implied by a small hand shape at the edge of frame holding something, but the primary visual field is the luminous squares. The geometry is the event.

children.name: Tesla_Household_Coat_Hook_1863
children.physique: Camera close on the wooden hook mounted by the door of the Tesla farmhouse. Dane's coat hanging from it — simple dark wool, worn at the elbows where the fabric has thinned from daily contact. The coat hangs slightly differently now — not because the hook has changed or the coat has changed, but because the person who will take it down is no longer coming. The wood of the hook, the rough whitewashed wall behind it, the edge of the door frame visible at one side. Nothing else in frame. The coat and the absence that is now inside it.
children.notes: Close shot — the hook is the full composition. No other objects compete. The coat must read as waiting for something that will not come.

children.name: Tesla_Household_Shoes_By_Door_1863
children.physique: Camera close on worn leather shoes placed beside the door of the Tesla farmhouse. The slight asymmetry of how Dane stood pressed permanently into the leather — heel worn more on the outside edge, the arch shaped by years of a specific body's weight distribution, the toe box holding the impression of toes that will not return. The stone floor around them cold and plain. The bottom edge of the door visible above. Other family shoes nearby at the edge of frame, for scale — but the camera is on Dane's shoes, and the difference between shoes that are still being used and shoes that are waiting is visible.
children.notes: Companion shot to the coat hook. Shoes at floor level — camera may angle slightly down. The specificity of one person's wear pattern in the leather is the image.

children.name: Tesla_Household_Wrong_Room_1863
children.physique: A room in the Tesla farmhouse after Dane's death. The same rough stone walls, low timber ceiling, familiar furniture in familiar positions — but the proportions are wrong. Not smaller. Wrong. Too large in a way that has nothing to do with measurement. Nikola, age 7 to 8, standing in the room — slight build, dark hair, still, not looking at anything in particular. The coat hook visible through an open doorway in the background. Light falling through a window with the quality of a room that has been emptied of something it cannot name. The wrongness is spatial — the room announces it.
children.notes: The most abstract of the Smiljan sub-locations. The wrongness must be achieved through composition and light, not distortion. The room is physically unchanged. The proportions feel wrong because something that filled them is no longer filling them.

assets.name: Gospic_Valley_1856
assets.physique: Valley town 15 kilometers below Smiljan on the limestone karst road. The valley floor visible from the plateau above. Open fields surrounding the town. Livestock normally pressed against fences and enclosures during storms. The morning after the birth storm: open fields with livestock standing in the open, all facing the same direction. The light that morning described as an examination being conducted — very white and particular, not the ordinary summer light of the Lika region.
assets.notes: Where Zdravko Blazic kept his diary and the Austrian Imperial Meteorological Institute maintained an observation station. Parent location — use sub-locations for all scene-level shots.

children.name: Blazic_Schoolhouse_1856
children.physique: Camera framed on a writing desk by a window in Blazic's quarters — a schoolteacher's private room in Gospic. The desk surface: ink, quill, a diary open to a freshly written entry. The handwriting patient, meticulous, the script of a man who records the observable world for its own sake. The window facing the valley fields where the livestock stood. The predawn light outside the window becoming the strange examination-quality morning light of July 11, 1856 — very white and particular, visible through the glass.
children.notes: Where Blazic recorded his observations of the livestock, the well water, and the light quality the morning after Tesla's birth.

children.name: Austrian_Meteorological_Station_1856
children.physique: Camera framed on the open log book lying on the writing surface of the observation station. Standard printed columns filled with careful bureaucratic handwriting — atmospheric pressure, temperature, precipitation, all recorded in the standard observer's hand and pen. In the margin of the July 11 entry: a notation in a visibly different hand, different pen, different pressure on the nib. The anomalous reading, written by someone who did not sign and never followed up. The instruments on stands visible in the background — barometer, thermometer mounted on the wall — and through the small window, the Gospic valley with the morning light that is the subject of the notation.
children.notes: The margin note reads: atmospheric ionization reading anomalous this morning. Instrument rechecked. No instrument fault found. Will report if anomaly continues. There is no follow-up entry.

children.name: Gospic_Valley_Fields_Dawn_1856
children.physique: Wide establishing shot: open fields on the valley floor below Smiljan at dawn on July 11, 1856. The storm has passed completely — the sky clear, the air still. The light carries a quality described as an examination — very white and particular, not the warm amber of ordinary Lika summer mornings. Livestock standing in the open fields, every animal oriented the same direction — not east, not toward shelter, not toward town. Facing the same way, as if addressed. Fences and enclosures visible at the field edges but unused — the animals have moved into the open voluntarily. Morning mist low on the karst limestone. The examination-light falling on every surface with equal, assessing weight.
children.notes: Blazic recorded this at dawn. Wide shot — the scale of the livestock behavior needs space to read. The direction every animal faces is the detail that must be compositionally clear.

children.name: Gospic_Well_1856
children.physique: Camera framed on a stone-walled well in the valley below Smiljan, the morning of July 11, 1856. Blazic drawing water — the rope, the wooden bucket descending and returning. The water in the bucket has a taste that was not there yesterday: sharper, more present, as if the water had acquired something overnight or shed something that had been buffering it. Dawn light falling on the well stones, the karst plateau visible in the background across the valley. The fields visible beyond — the livestock still in the open, still facing the same direction, visible at distance.
children.notes: The well water tasting different is one of Blazic's three observations. This shot grounds the abstract (examination light, directional livestock) in the physical and intimate — the taste of water drawn from a specific well on a specific morning.

assets.name: Hotel_St_Regis_1922
assets.physique: Where Tesla was living in 1922 when the white pigeon died in his hands. He was at the St. Regis before further financial unraveling brought him eventually to the Hotel New Yorker.
assets.notes: Parent location — use sub-locations for all scene-level shots.

children.name: St_Regis_Tesla_Holding_Pigeon_1922
children.physique: Camera framed on Tesla in his mid-60s, seated or standing in his hotel room, holding the dying white pigeon. Large aged hands cradling a small white body with grey-tipped wings — the grip careful, both palms making a cup. The bird's weight still warm, still the weight of a living thing making the small continuous adjustments of being held. The room behind him ordinary: hotel furniture, window light from a 1920s New York afternoon. The moment is still. The light in the room is normal. The light has not yet happened.
children.notes: The before-the-light shot. The pigeon is still alive and being held. The room is ordinary. Nothing in frame indicates what is about to occur.

children.name: St_Regis_Pigeon_Light_1922
children.physique: The same room in the moment the light comes from the pigeon's eyes. More powerful and blinding than anything Tesla had produced in his laboratory — the room is transformed by a light source that should not exist in an ordinary hotel room. Tesla's face illuminated from below and ahead by the light from his cupped hands. The walls, the ceiling, the furniture — all lit by a source that is the size of a small bird. His hands holding what is in the process of changing from held to carried. The light so intense it overwhelms the ordinary illumination of the room entirely.
children.notes: The light is the event. This may require treating as a near-atmosphere scene — the light is the primary subject, not the room or the bird as object. Tesla's face lit from below by the impossible light source.

children.name: St_Regis_Window_1922
children.physique: Camera framed on the window of Tesla's room at the St. Regis. The windowsill where the white pigeon made a habit of arriving. The view through the glass: 1920s New York, the street below, the geometry of the city. The window slightly open — kept open as a habit, for the bird who has not yet stopped coming. Perhaps breadcrumbs or small traces of seed on the outer sill. The glass and the frame and the curtain pulled aside with the specific arrangement of a window that has been opened and closed daily for a bird. The quality of a space maintained in readiness for a visitor.
children.notes: After the pigeon's death, this window would have remained, the habit of opening it perhaps continuing for some time. For the 1922 scene, the window is still in the period when the pigeon still came.

assets.name: Port_Of_New_York_1884
assets.physique: The immigration arrival area at Castle Garden, New York Harbor, June 1884. Wooden docks, iron railings, the bustle of immigrant processing. A tall young man of 28 with sharp features stepping onto American soil. Four cents in his pocket. A letter of introduction folded in his coat. The harbor behind him — tall-masted ships, steam vessels, the skyline of lower Manhattan. The specific weight of arriving somewhere with nothing but the contents of your own mind.
assets.notes: Tesla arrived June 6, 1884. He had been running machines in his mind for years before this crossing — complete, functional, mechanical systems operated entirely behind his eyes. He carried almost nothing physical. The letter was to Thomas Edison. Parent location — use sub-locations for scene-level shots.

children.name: Castle_Garden_Dock_1884
children.physique: Camera framed on the immigration dock at Castle Garden, June 1884. Wooden planks underfoot, iron railings along the dock edge, the organized press of immigrant processing — officials, queues, the noise of a processing facility handling the scale of 1884 immigration. A tall young man of 28 with sharp angular features stepping from gangplank to American soil — the specific moment of foot touching the dock. Four cents. A folded letter in his coat. The harbor behind him: tall-masted ships, steam vessels, the specific maritime density of New York Harbor in 1884. The weight of arriving with nothing physical except internal architecture.
children.notes: The arrival moment. Castle Garden was the immigration processing center before Ellis Island opened in 1892. In 1884, arrivals came through Castle Garden at the southern tip of Manhattan.

children.name: Port_Manhattan_Skyline_1884
children.physique: Wide establishing shot from the dock looking toward lower Manhattan across the harbor. The 1884 skyline: church spires dominating, the Brooklyn Bridge completed just one year prior in 1883 visible across the East River, no skyscrapers — the tallest structures still masonry, still vertical by weight of stone rather than steel frame. The harbor busy with maritime traffic in every direction. Morning light on the water. The city that Tesla's alternating current would eventually wire — here still gas-lit, still waiting, the infrastructure not yet built that his mind was already building behind his eyes.
children.notes: The 1884 skyline is specific and verifiable. The Brooklyn Bridge opened May 24, 1883 — it would be the most dramatic structure visible from the harbor one year after opening. No skyscrapers yet — the Home Insurance Building in Chicago was under construction, but New York's steel-frame era had not yet arrived.

assets.name: Wardenclyffe_Evidence_1943
assets.physique: Not Wardenclyffe Tower itself — but the evidence of Wardenclyffe found in Room 3327 and among the seized materials. Architectural drawings on yellowed paper. Correspondence with J.P. Morgan. Financial records. Photographs. All found among Tesla's papers, all part of what was seized and reviewed.
assets.notes: MANIFEST-ONLY RULE: Wardenclyffe Tower is not a visitable location in this episode. It is referenced only through documents, drawings, and photographs found in manifest locations — Room 3327 and the seized trunks. Show the evidence of Wardenclyffe, not Wardenclyffe itself. Parent location — use sub-locations for scene-level shots.

children.name: Wardenclyffe_Architectural_Drawings_1943
children.physique: Camera framed on large yellowed paper sheets laid out on a surface — part of Tesla's seized materials. Architectural plans for a tower designed to transmit power wirelessly across the planet. The distinctive mushroom-shaped copper dome sketched in precise engineering detail atop the skeletal wooden framework — the shape immediately recognizable. Measurements in Tesla's own handwriting in the margins. Fold lines showing the paper was stored rolled for decades. The drawings laid partially flat, partially still curling at the edges. The surface beneath them — a government examination table, or still partially rolled in a wooden crate beside an open trunk.
children.notes: The architectural drawings are the physical evidence of the concept. The mushroom dome is the distinctive shape. The handwriting in the margins is Tesla's — specific, not printed.

children.name: Morgan_Correspondence_1943
children.physique: Camera framed on letters on J.P. Morgan letterhead found among Tesla's papers. Heavy cream stock, engraved letterhead, the formal typeface of financial power in the early 1900s. The handwriting of someone whose correspondence was an institutional act. The pages aged and faded, the ink darkened to brown at the edges where light has touched it for forty years. The correspondence showing — across multiple letters laid out together — the gap between what was agreed (wireless communication) and what Tesla actually built (wireless power transmission for the planet). The tone visible even in the formality: early letters of investment, later letters of refusal.
children.notes: The Morgan correspondence is the paper record of the deal that was made and the deal that was not kept — or depending on interpretation, the deal Tesla expanded beyond without informing his investor.

children.name: Trump_Review_Documents_1943
children.physique: Camera framed on assessment papers from John G. Trump's review — the official government evaluation of Tesla's sixty years of work. Typed government forms on standard federal paper stock, classification stamps in red ink, the language of institutional judgment visible in partial: the phrase 'did not include new sound workable principles' readable on one page. Three days — or three weeks — to review sixty years of work. The documents carry the weight of a conclusion reached by a process and an institution, not by one man alone. Filed, stamped, classified.
children.notes: Trump reviewed the material over approximately three weeks, not three days (three days was the initial examination period). The conclusion — harmless, no new workable principles — was then followed by decades of classification. The documents are the record of that judgment.

assets.name: Macak_The_Cat_1859
assets.physique: Large Serbian farm tomcat. Dark-striped fur, heavy body. Back broad enough for a three-year-old to press both hands flat against. In darkness, the fur erupts with a continuous sheet of blue-white sparks fanning from the base of the tail to the neck when stroked — illuminating the child's finger bones from beneath for one instant before returning to darkness.
assets.notes: The family cat. Mačak is the Serbian word for tomcat. The discharge from his fur is what prompted Milutin Tesla to name electricity for his son for the first time.

assets.name: White_Pigeon_1922
assets.physique: A white pigeon, pure white with light grey tips on her wings. Small body — lighter than appearance suggests, the feathers making the size while the body beneath is much smaller. She made a habit of Tesla's window and returned daily. When dying: held in two large aged hands, the small body still warm, the grey-tipped wings spread slightly, the eyes producing a light more intense than any lamp in Tesla's laboratory.
assets.notes: Tesla described her to biographer O'Neill: a beautiful bird, pure white with light grey tips on her wings. He described finding recognition in her gaze — the only recognition in 86 years of looking. He loved her as a man loves a woman, and she loved him. When she died, something went out of my life. And then: Up to that time I knew with a certainty that I would complete my work.

assets.name: Three_Gray_Tipped_Feathers_1943
assets.physique: Three feathers on the windowsill of Room 3327. Each feather primarily white with gray tips. They do not lie as if drifted there or shed casually. They lie at angles relative to each other that suggest placement — deliberate, considered arrangement.
assets.notes: Found by Alice Monaghan when she entered Room 3327 on January 8, 1943. The white pigeon had been dead for approximately 20 years. The feathers were on the windowsill despite the window being closed and undisturbed.

assets.name: Tesla_Hotel_Napkin_Equations_1943
assets.physique: Dozens of white hotel napkins covered in dense mathematical notation in pencil — equations in a handwriting that crosses the printed borders of the napkins without adjusting, that treats the paper's edge as a limit the mind declined to recognize. Found on the desk, the bedside table, and the floor beside the bed. The equations are real mathematics — active scientific work, not scribbling.
assets.notes: Tesla used hotel napkins as his primary writing surface in his final years. The work showed no mental deterioration. The equations crossed the paper's edges as if the physical limits of the surface were irrelevant to the thinking being recorded.

assets.name: Tesla_Seized_Trunks_1943
assets.physique: Twenty trunks — worn leather steamer trunks with brass clasps, reinforced wooden crates bound with wire, cardboard filing boxes. Mixed sizes. Labels in mixed English and Serbian handwriting in Tesla's personal shorthand, dates spanning six decades. The accumulated output of a working mind that had not stopped until it stopped entirely: notes, designs, private correspondence, objects of investigation.
assets.notes: Seized by the Office of Alien Property Custodian within approximately two days of Tesla's death. Reviewed by John G. Trump in three weeks. Declared harmless. Then classified for decades.

assets.name: OAPC_Pre_Labeled_Crates_1943
assets.physique: New wooden shipping crates of raw unfinished pine slats, splintery. Stamped with official government markings in black ink: OFFICE OF ALIEN PROPERTY. Serial numbers. Pre-labeled before Tesla's death — the dimensions calibrated for what they intended to take, as if the inventory had been measured in advance.
assets.notes: The agents arrived with these crates already prepared and labeled. Empty. Already fitted for transport. Pre-labeling crates is not a response to death — it is preparation for an expected event.

assets.name: Blazic_Diary_1856
assets.physique: A handwritten diary, leather-bound, pages filled with a schoolteacher's careful script. The writing has the patient texture of a man recording the observable world for its own sake — weather, road conditions, livestock counts. One page water-damaged, the date partially illegible. A July 1856 entry describing livestock behavior, well water taste, and the examination-quality light of the morning of July 11. Transcribed in a 1931 regional folklore pamphlet that exists in no national archive.
assets.notes: Zdravko Blazic's diary. The July 1856 entry was written quickly, before the mind's need for explanation could smooth the image into comfort. He wrote it and moved to the next day's entry: road conditions.

assets.name: Atmospheric_Ionization_Log_1856
assets.physique: A formal observation log from the Austrian Imperial Meteorological Institute's Gospic station. Standard printed columns for atmospheric pressure, temperature, and precipitation filled in with careful bureaucratic handwriting. In the margin of the July 11, 1856 entry: a notation in a different hand, different pen, different pressure on the nib — written by someone who did not sign. The margin notation is the only anomaly in an otherwise standard record.
assets.notes: The margin note reads: Atmospheric ionization reading anomalous this morning. Instrument rechecked. No instrument fault found. Will report if anomaly continues. There is no follow-up entry. The note was written by a second observer who did not sign and never followed up.

assets.name: Dane_Coat_On_Hook_1863
assets.physique: A boy's coat hanging on a wooden hook by the door of the Tesla farmhouse. Simple dark wool, worn at the elbows, the fabric holding the shape of shoulders that wore it daily. It hangs slightly differently now — not because the hook has changed or the coat has changed, but because the person who will take it down is no longer coming to take it down. The absence has gotten into the coat. It has affected its relationship with gravity.
assets.notes: Dane Tesla's coat. After his death, it remained on the hook. The script uses it as the central image for how grief changes ordinary objects — not through any visible alteration, but through the withdrawal of the future that gave them purpose.

assets.name: Dane_Worn_Shoes_1863
assets.physique: A pair of worn leather shoes beside the door of the Tesla farmhouse. Broken in exactly the way one person's foot breaks leather — the slight asymmetry of how Dane stood, the particular weight distribution of how he walked, the specific shape of heel and arch and toe pressed into the leather over years of wearing. The shoes have learned their wearer. They hold the shape of someone who is not there.
assets.notes: Dane's shoes. Shoes learn their wearer with the patience of an object that spends years in close contact with a specific body. The body was not coming back. The shoes did not know this.

assets.name: Tesla_Tin_Fork_1862
assets.physique: A tin dinner fork, heavy for a child's hand. Slightly warm from being held. The seam where the handle was joined to the tines detectable under the thumb — a small ridge the thumb finds and returns to. Cold on the first touch, body-warm within sixty seconds. An ordinary object with the specific weight of the ordinary world — the last thing the six-year-old Tesla held before the geometry vision replaced his entire visual field.
assets.notes: The fork from the geometry vision scene. Tesla was holding it when his visual field was replaced by blinding light and then luminous geometric squares. The fork was still in his hand when he returned. The tactile world had not gone anywhere. Only the visual field had been replaced.

assets.name: Do_Not_Disturb_Sign_1943
assets.physique: A standard Hotel New Yorker cardboard door hanger, slightly curved from years of hanging. Dark printed border, the hotel's art deco design. Hanging from the brass door handle of Room 3327. It had been there since approximately January 5 — three days. The guest management record noted that the occupant had not requested food, laundry, or any contact whatsoever. This was known to be a preference. Longstanding. Staff had been told.
assets.notes: Three days on the door. The sign is both a practical hotel object and the first piece of evidence — the first indicator that something had changed behind this door. Staff knew not to disturb. But three days was three days.

assets.name: Tesla_Letter_Of_Introduction_1884
assets.physique: A folded letter on cream-colored paper, handwritten, addressed as an introduction to Thomas Edison. The paper worn at the folds from being carried in a coat pocket across an Atlantic crossing. The handwriting of someone who expected this letter to open a door. Alongside it: four American cents — the total cash Tesla carried when he arrived at the Port of New York on June 6, 1884.
assets.notes: Tesla arrived with four cents and this letter. He had been running machines in his mind for years before the crossing — complete, functional, mechanical systems operated entirely behind his eyes. The letter was his only physical credential. Everything else was internal.

assets.name: Birthing_Room_Headboard_Rail_1856
assets.physique: A wooden headboard rail on a simple bed in the Tesla birthing room. Dark timber, worn smooth where hands have gripped it. Duka Tesla's grip marks — not the grip of a frightened woman but of someone doing something with all of themselves. The wood shows the impression of fingers that held with a focus the midwife recognized as total commitment. Sparks from the charged air occasionally jumping to the wood surface.
assets.notes: The headboard rail Duka gripped during labor. The script describes her grip as requiring everything available — the grip of commitment, not fear. The midwife's hands found their positions. The work was clear, even when the room was wrong.

assets.name: FBI_Declassified_Tesla_File_1943
assets.physique: A thick government file, more than three hundred pages. Manila folder with typed labels, classification stamps, and declassification markings. Pages of typed reports, handwritten notes, memoranda between agencies. The FBI's file on Nikola Tesla — publicly available through the FBI's online FOIA reading room. The pages carry the institutional weight of a government that seized eighty trunks of material, declared it harmless, and then classified it for decades.
assets.notes: The FBI's declassified Tesla file runs more than 300 pages. Anyone can read it. The individual contents of the approximately eighty trunks and crates remained classified for decades. Harmless things are not classified.
